notice: Curated source-backed reports, separate from synthetic scenarios and newly collected signals. Dates and jurisdictions matter; these records are not a current product-wide safety verdict.

cases.title: Cattle-feed bran in biscuits: what the records say.
cases.summary: FSSAI findings reported in October 2026 concerned cattle-feed bran used as a fibre ingredient in Priyagold biscuits. Nepal subsequently issued an import suspension and recall notice.
findings: Nepal's official notice cites an FSSAI communication dated 17 October about material marked for cattle feed, alongside hygiene deficiencies.
The Nepal order covers all batches and production dates of the specified manufacturer's biscuits within its jurisdiction.
cases.company_response: A manufacturer response was not established in the sources reviewed for this profile.
cases.limitations: Reports describe cattle-feed bran. Proceedings and licence action are distinct from a final court judgment. The linked sources do not identify a specific affected Indian batch.

cases.title: A fresh label doesn't make old stock fresh.
cases.summary: Delhi reporting described a warehouse operation allegedly replacing dates on expired or near-expiry soft drinks and biscuits. Police seized stock and reported three arrests.
findings: The Times of India reported altered dates and batch information on packaged goods in a Dwarka warehouse.
ThePrint separately described date-erasing and reprinting equipment in the reported operation.
cases.company_response: These reports concern alleged downstream relabelling. No manufacturer-wide finding is established by this profile.
cases.limitations: A police allegation is not a conviction. This is a dated local supply-chain case, not a recall of every product sold under the named beverage brands.

cases.title: The spice recall that crossed borders.
cases.summary: Hong Kong's CFS reported ethylene oxide in specified MDH and Everest spice mixes in April 2024. An Australian recall separately covered Everest Fish Curry Masala 50 g.
findings: The CFS notice identifies four products, date markings and instructions to withdraw affected stock.
The Australian notice identifies the 50 g product with a September 2025 best-before date.
cases.company_response: Manufacturer responses are not reproduced here; the original notices establish the recalled products and markets.
cases.limitations: This is a 2024 historical case. Its product and date limits must not be presented as a current recall of all Indian MDH or Everest products.
